title: Week 3: Cut the cord
summary: An Anker 20,000 mAh battery takes over from the wall plug, so your robot runs with no cables at all. Then pick it up and take it for a walk.
detail: Mount the battery pack in the bottom of the box, move the Pi's power onto it, and check everything still runs. Then the robot is fully wireless: carry it across the room and keep talking.
outcome: A cardboard robot that runs anywhere on its own battery, listening, talking and moving its mouth.
prereqs: Your robot from Week 2, with its Raspberry Pi.
Your laptop, for the Pi's remote link.
On your table: an Anker 20,000 mAh power bank and a short USB-C cable.

slides.title: Week 3: Cut the cord
bullets: Then pick it up and walk around with it.

slides.title: What each robot needs this week
bullets: ☐ Your robot from Week 2, with its Pi, speakerphone and Pico
☐ 1 × Anker 20,000 mAh power bank, fully charged
☐ 1 × short USB-C to USB-C cable, battery to Pi
☐ Velcro strips or tape, to hold the battery in the box
Bring: your laptop and your Deepgram key
slides.note: Keep the power banks: they stay with the robots for Week 4, where they also power the neck. The Pi 4 wants a steady 3 A. If a Pi shows a lightning bolt or restarts on battery, swap to a port marked for higher power or a thicker cable. Charge every power bank the night before. Helper table: spare charged power banks and spare short USB-C cables.

slides.title: Mount the battery
bullets: Charge check: press the button on the power bank, all lights should show.
Slide the battery into the bottom of the box, behind the servo.
Tape it down so it can't slide around.
slides.note: The battery is the heaviest part, so low in the box keeps the robot from tipping.

slides.title: Move the power over
bullets: Plug the Pi's power cable into the battery's USB-C port.
Unplug the wall supply. Everything should keep running.
Pick the robot up and carry it to another table. Keep talking.
slides.note: Done when: the wall plug is out and the robot still answers.

slides.title: Week 4: give it a neck
bullets: A second box, a servo and a lazy-susan bearing.
The head turns and looks around while it talks.
Keep the battery in. The neck runs on it too.

flow.title: Final test, unplugged
flow.note: Open this page on the robot's Pi. Unplug the wall supply, then start talking.

troubleshooting: The Pi restarts when the mouth moves: the battery port can't keep up. Try the battery's other port, or a thicker cable.
The Pi shows a lightning bolt: the battery is low or the cable is thin. Charge the battery or swap the cable.
The battery switches itself off: some power banks sleep on low current. Press its button to wake it.
